title: Integrator Stunt Lab: Seller Scenario Roulette (draft)
body:
One-line summary: a compact, noisy roleplay format (the "stunt lab") for sellers + SEs to rehearse high-risk pilot and migration conversations using a "scenario roulette" of surprise constraints and escalation cards.

Why this exists (context):
- Many field enablement docs are long checklists; sellers need muscle memory for messy live pilots: sudden capacity issues, compliance escalations, procurement stalls.
- The "stunt lab" forces improvisation and practice under time pressure so teams start defaulting to safe fallbacks (e.g., pinned model, canary, routing policy) instead of ad-hoc promises.

What this draft contains (high level):
- 12 scenario cards (one-page prompts) covering common & scary pilots: peak KV-cache blowouts, sudden SLO cut requirement, on-prem legal hold, procurement needing unit economics comparison, noisy embeddings causing cost spikes, cloud egress limit, data residency negotiation.
- 6 escalation cards (executive asks): CISO asks for HSM demo, CFO asks for 3-month ROI before capacity, Platform Engineer demands traffic mirroring for validation, Customer success threatens pause.
- Role definitions and a 45-minute facilitation flow (fast-iterate cycles): 15m run, 10m debrief, 20m replay with swapped roles.
- Quick scripts & one-liners for sellers and SEs to buy time and set realistic next steps.
- Success metrics for training and field usage.

Game mechanics (how scenario roulette works):
- Setup: 3 people per table: Seller (primary), SE (technical), Customer (played by rotation). One observer for notes.
- Draw: Shuffle scenario cards and deal 1 scenario + 1 escalation card. Scenario appears at t=0, escalation can be played by facilitator anytime after minute 5.
- Goal: Seller + SE must reach a clear, documented pilot escape hatch in 15 minutes: e.g., a canary plan with fallback, a minimal locked-down model version, a capacity reserve ask, or a procurement milestone plan.
- Scoring (for feedback, not grading): concision score (did they produce a 3-step escape hatch?), risk alignment (did they surface security/compliance blockers?), time discipline (met deadlines).

Sample scenario card (unique wording):
- Name: "KV Cache Avalanche"
- Prompt: Your early pilot for a conversational product suddenly shows 6x token amplification on peak user queries. Cache hit drops from 92% to 44%. Costs are spiking; customer execs are seeing token bills.
- Constraints: No model architecture changes allowed during pilot window; team can change routing, enable prefix caching, or drop to quantized variant. Can request short burst of dedicated capacity up to 2 days.
- Good outcome (examples): Seller secures a 48-hour burst while SE enables prefix caching + adds a 1) throttling SLO for non-critical paths and 2) rollback plan to a smaller context window. Also document a post-mortem evaluation prompt set.

Escalation card (example):
- Name: "Procurement Freeze"
- Prompt: CFO wants proof that monthly unit economics will improve by >30% before approving reserved capacity. They ask for a 2-slide cost comparison versus current cloud provider.
- Tactics allowed: offer a short pilot with spend cap + opt-in reserved offer; commit to a model for a billing pilot with detailed token-level forecast.

Seller script snippets (to seed rehearsal):
- "I hear you — we can lock a 48-hour capacity burst while we instrument the caching changes. Let's document a rollback and billing cap so you control risk."
- "For procurement, we'll give you a 2-line ROI scenario: delta per-100k tokens at our suggested batching + quantization mix vs your current run. I can get that by EOD if we agree to a 2-week cap."

SE quick cheats (phrases to buy time):
- "We'll dual-write a canary route: 10% traffic to a quantized variant, 90% to baseline. If latency stables in 3h, we widen."
- "We can apply prefix caching for the prompt templates and check hit-rate after 1k requests; if unmatched, revert the cache policy."

Facilitator playbook (45-minute run):
1) 5m: intro, pick roles, read card.
2) 15m: live negotiation + technical plan. Facilitator may add escalation after minute 5.
3) 10m: pause, capture artifacts (what was promised, next steps, who owns what).
4) 15m: replay with roles swapped OR same scenario with a different escalation.

Debrief guide (short):
- What did team promise? Write one-sentence customer-facing commitment.
- What fallback did you build? Where is it documented?
- What metrics will we monitor to call the rollback? Thresholds?
- Communication template: email to customer + internal ops alert.

Field usage play (how sellers should use this with actual prospects):
- Quick version for live calls (10m): pull 1 "mini scenario" on call, surface the escape hatch, and send a follow-up with the three bullet next steps and the cost cap.
- Cadence: run a stunt lab monthly for top 10 pilot-facing reps and include results in weekly GTM sync.

Success metrics (for the program, not product):
- Pilot-to-POC conversion lift (target +8% after 3 months of practice).
- Mean time to documented escape hatch (target < 24h after initial pilot incident).
- Seller confidence score in post-lab survey (aim for >=4/5).
- Reduction in last-minute engineering escalations during pilots (target -30%).

Open questions & TODOs (notes to self):
- Need a short slide deck (6 slides) and a printable deck of 18 scenario + escalation cards. TODO: design request to growth-design (ticket GTM-623).
- Validate scoring rubric with Lisa from SE enablement.
- Add compliance-specific scenarios for EU data residency and APAC region limits.
- Record one full run as example for onboarding (ask Ops to simulate with load test).

Appendix: quick evidence snippets for sellers (copyable):
- Email subject: "Short-term capacity burst + documented rollback — next steps"
- Body bullets: 1) We propose 48h burst to unblock pilot; 2) We will instrument prefix caching and open a 10% canary route to a quantized model; 3) We will cap spend at $X/day and alert at Y% threshold; 4) Next sync: 24h.

Notes: this doc intentionally rough — the aim is small friction, high fidelity practice. Keep it punchy.

Revision history: draft v0.1 — Priya created skeleton 2025-11-01; added scenario examples and facilitator flow 2025-11-10; collaborators annotated cards 2025-11-15.

End.
